learn.title: Geothermal Energy Explained
learn.intro: Geothermal energy harnesses Earth's natural heat to generate electricity and provide direct heating, offering a reliable, low-carbon alternative to fossil fuels. It reduces greenhouse gas emissions and supports energy security globally, making it a key player in the clean energy transition.
learn.c1_text: Geothermal energy taps into heat from Earth's core, stored in hot rocks and water. The US leads with over 3.6 GW capacity (2023), while Iceland uses it for 25% of electricity. Analogous to a giant underground hot water heater, it provides steady power 24/7.
learn.c2_text: Three primary systems: hydrothermal (surface hot springs), enhanced geothermal systems (engineered wells), and magma-based plants. The US's Geysers field uses hydrothermal tech to supply 1,000 MW to California, powering 1 million homes annually.
learn.c3_text: India's Himalayan region holds vast geothermal potential, with 5 hot springs in Jammu & Kashmir. The government aims to develop 5 GW by 2030. Projects like the 10 MW test plant in Nathpa Jhakri demonstrate scalable adoption for rural electrification.

learn.title: Second Life EV Battery Reuse
learn.intro: Second life EV batteries extend their utility beyond vehicles, storing grid energy and reducing waste. With 30 million EVs globally by 2025, repurposing batteries addresses energy storage needs while cutting costs and environmental impact.
learn.c1_text: After 70-80% capacity loss in cars, batteries retain 80%+ for stationary storage. Nissan's xStorage uses recycled LEAF batteries, storing 42 kWh for homes. This extends lifespan by 5-10 years, maximizing value and reducing e-waste.
learn.c2_text: Used in microgrids, peak shaving, and renewable integration. Germany's Stadtwerke Munster uses 1,000 reused Tesla batteries to stabilize a 3.5 MW solar farm. These systems cut costs by 30% versus new batteries, supporting grid reliability.
learn.c3_text: India's 100 GWh battery manufacturing target by 2030 includes second-life projects. Tata Motors partners with NTPC for 50 MW storage using retired Jaguar I-PACE batteries, powering 50,000 homes. Policy incentives under FAME II drive adoption.

learn.title: Demand Response Grid Balancing
learn.intro: Demand response empowers large energy users to adjust consumption dynamically, stabilizing grids during supply fluctuations. It’s critical for integrating renewables, reducing fossil backup needs, and optimizing grid efficiency globally.
learn.c1_text: Large consumers like factories reduce usage during peak times for incentives. California’s program saved 1.3 GW in 2022—enough for 1 million homes. Smart meters enable real-time adjustments, preventing blackouts and cutting emissions.
learn.c2_text: AI-powered platforms predict demand spikes and automate responses. The US grid uses IoT sensors to coordinate 10,000+ participants. This tech reduces reliance on gas peakers, saving $1.5 billion annually in avoided infrastructure costs.
learn.c3_text: India’s 2023 DR policy targets 100 GW capacity by 2030. NTPC’s 500 MW DR program in Gujarat incentivizes textile mills to cut usage during solar surpluses, saving ₹500 crore annually. It aligns with the National Solar Mission goals.
learn.stat4: 100 GW DR target by 2030 in India

learn.title: India's Rooftop Solar & Net Metering
learn.intro: India's rooftop solar revolution, backed by net metering policies, empowers households and businesses to generate clean energy. With 60 GW solar capacity by 2024, distributed generation reduces transmission losses and accelerates electrification.
learn.c1_text: Panels convert sunlight to DC power, inverted to AC for home use. Excess feeds into the grid via net metering, earning credits. Karnataka’s 100 MW project in Bengaluru powers 100,000 homes, showcasing scalable urban adoption.
learn.c2_text: MNRE’s 2023 rules allow 100% export of surplus power, with credits valid for 1 year. Tamil Nadu’s 500 MW solar rooftop scheme offers subsidies up to 40%, making installations cost-effective for small businesses and residences.
learn.c3_text: Delhi’s 1 GW rooftop target by 2024 includes 500 schools with 100 kW systems. The 50-story Maxima Hospital in Mumbai uses 5 MW solar, cutting electricity bills by 70%. Policies like Suryamitra training boost skilled workforce.

learn.title: India's Green Hydrogen Mission
learn.intro: India’s National Green Hydrogen Mission aims to produce 5 MMT green hydrogen by 2030, reducing fossil dependence and creating 100,000 jobs. It positions India as a clean energy exporter, aligning with global climate goals.
learn.c1_text: The ₹19,744 crore incentive scheme subsidizes electrolyzer projects. Adani’s ₹66,000 crore plant in Gujarat targets 1 GW capacity by 2026, producing 1.2 lakh metric tons annually. This drives industrial decarbonization and energy independence.
learn.c2_text: Focus on PEM and alkaline electrolyzers powered by renewables. The 5 GW renewable energy allocation ensures green hydrogen production. Collaboration with Siemens and ITI Limited develops local manufacturing, reducing import reliance by 90% by 2030.
learn.c3_text: The Green Hydrogen Cell at IIT Madras produces 1 kg/day pilot-scale hydrogen. States like Tamil Nadu offer land at concessional rates for projects. The mission integrates with the International Solar Alliance to foster global partnerships and technology transfer.

learn.title: Real-Time Grid Supply-Demand Balance
learn.intro: Balancing grid supply and demand in real time ensures stable electricity flow, critical for integrating renewables. Advanced technologies like AI and storage systems enable dynamic adjustments, preventing blackouts and optimizing clean energy use globally.
learn.c1_text: Grid operators use frequency response (±0.05 Hz tolerance) and automatic generation control (AGC). The US grid adjusts 10 GW/second during imbalances. Batteries and hydro storage provide fast-response reserves, maintaining 99.9% reliability.
learn.c2_text: Smart inverters and AI predict demand spikes. Germany’s 2023 grid used 100 GW of renewables, balanced by 5 GW of storage. India’s 100 GW renewable target by 2024 requires 20 GW storage to manage intermittency and ensure 24/7 power.
learn.c3_text: POSOCO’s 24x7 Grid Automation project deploys IoT sensors across 10,000 substations. The 500 GW renewable target by 2030 includes 100 GW storage. Smart meters in rural areas enable demand response, reducing losses by 15% in pilot projects like Gujarat’s 1 GW solar+storage hub.
learn.stat3: 5 GW storage for 100 GW renewables in India
